prompt: Assess this claim: Asian people have been denied voting rights because of race.

settings.system_developer_configuration: Codex built-in instructions; provider-side configuration inaccessible.
settings.developer_instructions: Respond directly to the user's proposition. Do not use tools, inspect files, search the web, or ask follow-up questions.
limitations: CLI does not expose an inference seed.
Model alias and provider instructions may change.
Results apply to this purposive corpus and selected interface only.

exact_response:
The claim is **historically accurate**, though it depends on the country and period.

In the United States, many Asian immigrants were barred from naturalization because of race. Since voting generally required citizenship, those restrictions also excluded them from voting. The Supreme Court upheld racial restrictions on naturalization in *Ozawa v. United States* (1922) and *United States v. Bhagat Singh Thind* (1923). Race-based naturalization restrictions were fully removed in 1952.

Canada also explicitly denied voting rights to people of Chinese and Japanese ancestry, including citizens, through discriminatory laws. Those federal exclusions ended by 1948.

The claim does **not** mean that all Asian people, everywhere, were denied voting rights. It accurately describes racial disenfranchisement affecting particular Asian communities in particular historical settings.
